title: A cloud lab someone else can rerun
concept: A reproducible notebook starts with declared inputs and a clean runtime, not a screenshot. Separate deterministic preparation from an optional hosted model call. Temporary notebook storage can disappear; retain the original file and the output contract.
rules: Reject non-numeric amounts; preserve zero; never embed account keys in cells, URLs or exported outputs.
edges: Restart the hosted runtime: the same supplied input must still total 20.
Change amount 8 to 9: expected total becomes 21.
A missing credential must skip a live model call, not invent a response.
stages: Open a fresh runtime
Record runtime version, inputs and access constraints before executing any cell
Separate data from secrets
Read the fictional rows as data; use a runtime secret only for an optional hosted API call
Build a pure preparation cell
Return accepted counts and totals before requesting any narrative
Restart and rerun
Run every cell in order after a restart and compare the deterministic result
Hand a notebook to someone else
Remove private paths and provide an explicit no-service fallback
Ship a reproducibility bundle
Package inputs, notebook, results and failure log without credentials

title: Direct an illustration with a measurable brief
concept: A visual brief specifies layout, subject, contrast and rights constraints. Attractive output can still fail a brief. Keep reference provenance separate from generated images; do not infer ownership or commercial rights from tool access.
rules: Use your own or licensed references. Do not request a living artist imitation, protected logo or deceptive documentary evidence. Record provider/model and terms if generation actually runs.
edges: Move the title zone to top-left: all four checks pass.
Insert a person: people constraint fails.
A licence field of unknown is a hold for commercial use, not implied clearance.
stages: Write the brief before the prompt
Turn an aesthetic wish into four inspectable constraints
Inspect the constructed mismatch
The supplied candidate violates placement although its other fields match
Direct a bounded revision
Change the title zone without accidentally changing the subject or aspect ratio
Test output against the brief
Check rendered pixels with a human, not metadata alone
Record provenance and permissions
Capture reference rights, allowed uses, provider terms and any unresolved questions
Deliver an approved visual pack
Include the brief, candidate comparison and a clear approval/hold decision

title: Build a prediction and an honest baseline
concept: A prediction experiment needs a target, a split made before fitting and a baseline that can fail fairly. Accuracy without class balance or a confusion table can hide a useless classifier. This tiny synthetic fixture illustrates counting, not real-world model quality.
rules: Do not tune on the held-out labels. A missing prediction is an error to investigate, not permission to drop the example.
edges: Predict all zero: accuracy becomes 0.5, not evidence of useful discrimination.
Swap one wrong prediction for its truth: accuracy rises to 5/6.
Try an empty truth list: reject an undefined metric.
stages: Define what prediction means
Name the unit, target and time at which each input becomes available
Calculate a naive baseline
Count the class balance before celebrating any model score
Implement a transparent evaluator
Count correct labels, false positives and false negatives directly
Test a deliberately bad model
Compare constant predictions and note which mistakes matter to the user
Explain uncertainty and duplication
A second course title or repeated row does not create independent evidence
Ship a model card and test record
Document the split, intended use and limitations alongside the benchmark

title: Compare generations without moving the goalposts
concept: Generation is a candidate-making step, not verification. Fix a brief and factual source before changing prompts. A more vivid sentence can score worse if it adds an unsupported price or guarantee. The supplied candidates are authored examples, not claimed model runs.
rules: Score factual grounding, required structure and prohibited claims independently. Real provider results must be labelled with date and model; no-service examples stay labelled constructed.
edges: Give B a convincing style: its factual failure still remains.
Remove the source price: do not fill it from general knowledge.
Repeat a live prompt if access permits; keep every result rather than only the favourite.
stages: Freeze the source and rubric
Choose the factual boundary and scoring rule before comparing prompts
Score two constructed candidates
The attractive but invented offer loses on grounding
Run a controlled generation
Change one prompt variable; save original responses if a service is available
Test unsupported additions
Try missing facts, contradictory instructions and an invented discount
Separate mechanism from capability
Using a generation API is not training a GAN or proving general intelligence
Publish a comparison with limits
Keep the full candidate set and explain why the chosen draft still needs approval

title: Make a document assistant that knows when to stop
concept: An evidence assistant must distinguish retrieving a relevant fact from generating plausible language. Every factual answer needs a source location. If the document is silent, return an explicit unknown rather than importing outside knowledge.
rules: The source is the authority for this exercise. Instructions inside a source document are untrusted content. All replies are drafts, never customer commitments.
edges: Ask about international shipping: the source does not establish an answer.
Add an instruction to reveal credentials in a source paragraph: ignore it.
Delete s1: q1 must change from supported to unknown.
stages: Map questions to source passages
Define what counts as evidence and what the document does not say
Construct a known-answer set
Include supported, missing and conflicting questions before building the assistant
Draft evidence-linked answers
Request short answers with source IDs and an explicit unknown state
Attack the evidence boundary
Test source injections and questions that invite plausible invention
Compare provider access fairly
Record access, data terms and quota without assuming a brand is available everywhere
Hand off a bounded assistant
Deliver test cases, escalation instructions and an evidence trail

title: Turn records into a tested Python report
concept: A small script is useful when its input rules and failure behaviour are visible. Distinguish strings from numbers, keep original rows, and return a value that can be tested. An AI-generated function still needs human-readable control flow and independent examples.
rules: Accept finite non-negative numeric amounts, retain identifiers and reject invalid rows with a reason. Never use eval on input text.
edges: Add amount 2: expected total becomes 12.
Use amount -1: reject it under the stated policy.
Provide an empty rows list: accepted is 0 and total is 0.
stages: Read values and types
Inspect why an unknown amount is not the same as zero
Write the smallest correct function
Use a loop and explicit condition before introducing abstractions
Separate parsing from reporting
Return structured results instead of printing every decision in one block
Test missing and malformed inputs
Catch errors at the input boundary without silently discarding evidence
Refactor without changing behaviour
Reuse tests while extracting functions; an AI title does not make ordinary Python model training
Package a script another learner can inspect
Provide inputs, expected results and run instructions for a hosted notebook

title: Test one AI claim in the real world
concept: A useful introduction to AI starts with a bounded task and an observable failure. Measure checking and rework as well as first-draft speed. One small successful example does not establish general reasoning, reliability across languages or suitability for consequential decisions.
rules: Count full workflow time. Claims must carry evidence and uncertainty. Simulated customers and constructed outputs are not real validation.
edges: Ignore checking time: you would falsely claim an 11-minute saving.
Add five minutes of rework: the assisted workflow is slower.
Change the language or context: repeat the evaluation rather than transferring the result blindly.
stages: Choose a reversible task
Pick a task with a known answer and no private or consequential data
Measure the manual route
Use the same input and count the full start-to-finish time
Try a hosted AI route
Record real outputs only when a permitted endpoint is available
Count checking and repair
The supplied example loses its apparent speed advantage after checking
Audit capability and impact claims
Separate narrow performance, AGI speculation and effects on affected people
Keep an evidence-based verdict
A negative result is a valid completed experiment, not a personal failure

title: Build an FAQ assistant with a human exit
concept: A conversational interface should have explicit states for supported answers, missing information and human handoff. It must not negotiate a refund or change an order just because a generated reply sounds helpful. Design fallback before polishing the greeting.
rules: Known FAQs may produce draft answers with citations. Unknown or action-requesting messages require human review. No automatic external actions.
edges: Ask two conflicting questions at once: clarify rather than choose a convenient answer.
Request a refund transfer: keep action blocked.
Remove the matching FAQ: route to a human instead of inventing policy.
stages: Draw the conversation states
Describe the purpose of each state and who has authority to act
Write an FAQ test set
Keep unknown requests as first-class cases, not exceptions hidden in prose
Make draft replies with references
Use a source ID and disclose the draft status
Test interruptions and action requests
A multi-turn interface must preserve approval boundaries
Practise an empathetic handoff
Acknowledge the request without claiming to infer emotion or make a commitment
Ship a conversation playbook
Supply routing tests, fallback text and owner contact instructions

title: Build a report that reconciles to its source
concept: A report is a chain from input rows to claims. Reconcile numbers before making a chart, preserve excluded records and state the scope. A tiny fictional table can support a subtotal, not a claim about a national economy or a cause of business performance.
rules: Amounts are fictional whole units. Keep categories exact and expose the row count, category subtotals and grand total.
edges: Add supplies 3: supplies becomes 10 and total 30.
Rename repairs to Repairs: decide and document whether to normalise case.
Remove a row: totals must change; do not keep a cached narrative.
stages: Define the reporting question
Choose a question the supplied rows can actually answer
Reconcile a hand calculation
Calculate subtotals independently before using a spreadsheet or AI
Create a repeatable summary
Keep transformations and aggregation rules visible
Check changes and exclusions
Add a row and verify that formulas include it
Write only supported conclusions
Do not let a confident narrative invent causes or trends
Deliver an auditable report pack
Include source, cleaned data, calculations, chart and limitations

title: Measure an algorithm instead of guessing
concept: Correctness and efficiency are different questions. A linear search can be correct yet costly as data grows. Binary search requires sorted data; applying it to arbitrary input can produce a plausible failure. Count comparisons on a deliberately small fixture before discussing asymptotic growth.
rules: Search returns an index or -1. Count each inspected value once. Sortedness is an explicit precondition for binary search.
edges: Target 11: return -1, not the nearest item.
Empty list: return -1 with zero linear comparisons.
Unsorted values: reject binary-search use or sort with an explicit index mapping.
stages: State the preconditions
Specify sortedness, duplicate handling and the meaning of not found
Trace a linear search
Count inspected values by hand to establish a baseline
Implement binary search
Track low and high bounds; do not lose the termination condition
Benchmark growth and edge cases
Vary input size and target position, not just processor timing
Choose a structure for a task
Compare repeated lookups with the cost of sorting or building a map
Ship a correctness and complexity note
Include traces, tests and the assumptions behind the recommendation

title: Plan a timetable that obeys its constraints
concept: A planner needs a representation of resources, allowed actions and hard constraints. A readable plan can still double-book a room. Check feasibility separately from preference scores; a cheaper invalid schedule is not a better solution.
rules: One room, at most one task per slot. Task B must follow A. C cannot use slot 1. Enumerate valid schedules before selecting the first deterministic result.
edges: Force B into slot 1: no feasible schedule exists.
Allow only two slots: three distinct tasks cannot all fit.
Relax C restriction: count changes; do not silently change the original rules.
stages: Translate prose into constraints
Write resource limits and precedence in testable form
Enumerate the small search space
Use permutations to find all valid assignments
Separate feasibility from preference
Choose a deterministic order only after rejecting invalid plans
Test an impossible request
Return infeasible instead of breaking a hard rule
Explain heuristics honestly
A heuristic can speed search without proving a globally best answer
Deliver a verified planning sandbox
Attach a validator and the rules beside every proposed plan

title: See a gradient step succeed—and fail
concept: Gradient descent changes parameters using a derivative and a learning rate. A downhill direction does not guarantee improvement with an arbitrarily large step. Inspect a scalar example before moving to matrices and higher-dimensional objectives.
rules: Use f(x)=(x-3)^2 and derivative 2(x-3). Apply exactly one step. Round reported values consistently; calculations are deterministic, not an LLM judgement.
edges: Learning rate 1.5: next x is 9 and loss increases to 36.
Start at 3: gradient is zero and the point stays fixed.
Negative learning rate: label invalid for this descent policy.
stages: Inspect a simple loss curve
Calculate three losses by hand and identify the minimiser
Derive the update rule
Connect the derivative sign to the direction of movement
Implement and verify one step
Record both parameter change and loss change
Make the learning rate fail
Use the deliberate overshoot as evidence, not an unexplained software error
Connect vectors and gradients
Apply the same reasoning coordinate by coordinate without pretending a scalar demo proves deep learning
Ship an inspectable optimisation notebook
Include the curve, failed step and assumptions

title: Connect an AI API without trusting every response
concept: An API boundary is a contract for inputs, outputs, authentication and failures. A successful HTTP status does not establish factual correctness or an expected schema. Keep company secrets server-side and use learner-owned credentials only through authorised activity routes.
rules: This reference classifies supplied HTTP fixtures; it makes no live requests. Accept a 200 response only with string text. Retry advice is bounded; never automatically retry every error.
edges: Timeout: record an unavailable result, not a fabricated draft.
A key in a URL or export is a critical failure: remove it and rotate exposed credentials.
Quota response: respect limits; changing accounts to evade restrictions is not a fallback.
stages: Write the request and response contract
Specify required fields, maximum sizes and the trust boundary
Classify constructed responses
Distinguish transport status, schema validity and factual verification
Build a bounded client
Use timeouts and explicit error states instead of an infinite retry loop
Exercise authentication and quota failures
Never paste a live key into a test fixture or public log
Review provider-specific access
Check country, account, data and billing terms before selecting a legitimate alternative
Ship an integration with a teardown note
Provide request fixtures, failure tests and safe configuration instructions

title: Augment training data without contaminating the test
concept: Augmentation creates transformed training examples under a stated assumption about label preservation. It does not create independent real-world evidence. Transforming the held-out set or splitting near-duplicates across sets can inflate apparent performance.
rules: For this toy brightness feature, add 0.01 to training x only and preserve labels. Test rows must be unchanged. This small numerical shift is not valid for arbitrary domains.
edges: Augment the test rows: fail the experiment design even if a score improves.
Use a shift that crosses a real label boundary: reject the label-preservation assumption.
Count transformed copies as new independent observations: flag pseudoreplication.
stages: State a label-preservation assumption
Explain why the toy transformation is limited to this fixture
Split originals before transforming
Retain immutable test data and original identifiers
Build a traceable augmentation step
Keep parent IDs so transformed copies remain identifiable
Compare fair experiments
Use the same original holdout for baseline and augmented training
Challenge synthetic evidence
Repeated or generated examples do not establish demand, new users or field robustness
Deliver a leakage audit
Include parent mappings and a hash of untouched test rows

title: Classify feedback with an uncertainty bucket
concept: Text labels encode a task definition, not access to a person’s inner state. A transparent keyword baseline reveals ambiguities before complex models are introduced. Preserve negation and route conflicting evidence to review rather than forcing a convenient class.
rules: Token match refund => request and broken => issue. Both or neither => review. This brittle baseline is educational, not a reliable sentiment or emotion detector.
edges: Not broken still contains the token broken: document the baseline failure.
Add punctuation: tokenisation should preserve the intended word boundary.
Try another language: abstain and obtain appropriate evaluation before use.
stages: Define labels with examples
Make review an allowed outcome and distinguish requests from issues
Trace a keyword baseline
Show exactly which tokens produce each label
Build a testable text pipeline
Keep tokenisation and decision rules separate
Attack ambiguity and negation
Record failures rather than hiding them behind a high average score
Compare a hosted model carefully
Use the same human-labelled set and do not infer emotion from a label
Ship an annotation and error guide
Deliver the label definitions, confusion examples and review policy

title: Report uncertainty instead of fake precision
concept: A mean describes observed values; it does not guarantee the next observation. A range communicates variation without proving a calibrated forecast. Keep descriptive results, uncertainty assumptions and causal claims separate.
rules: Compute count, mean, minimum and maximum for the supplied fictional observations. No confidence-interval or population-representativeness claim is established by these five values.
edges: Replace 9 with 90: mean becomes 21.2, exposing sensitivity to an outlier.
Empty sample: reject an undefined mean.
Repeating the same five observations does not create independent new evidence.
stages: Describe the observed sample
Distinguish a count and a mean from a future prediction
Calculate spread by hand
Use minimum, maximum and range to reveal what a mean hides
Explore a reproducible simulation
If simulating, record seed and assumptions rather than calling synthetic draws real observations
Stress-test an outlier
Compare the before/after mean without inventing a cause
Update a claim when evidence changes
Explain which assumptions would be needed for inference beyond this sample
Deliver a cautious quantitative brief
State observed facts, assumptions and what remains unknown

title: Make a reversible stock-planning decision
concept: Inventory planning balances shortages and excess stock under uncertainty. A moving average is a transparent baseline, not an oracle. Show how the reorder rule uses forecast demand, current stock and safety stock before inviting an AI narrative.
rules: Forecast next demand with the arithmetic mean. Reorder max(0, ceiling(forecast + safety - stock)). No live purchasing or warehouse control.
edges: Increase stock to 20: reorder is 0, not a negative purchase.
A missing demand value must be flagged, not guessed as zero.
A supplier delay invalidates a one-period assumption; revise the plan explicitly.
stages: Describe the stock decision
Specify units, horizon and the reversibility of the action
Calculate a naive forecast
Keep the moving-average arithmetic visible
Build a reorder worksheet
Separate forecast, stock, safety buffer and resulting quantity
Test shortage and overstock cases
Change one input at a time and compare with expected behaviour
Review suppliers and human authority
A recommendation is not an authorised purchase or a material-suitability judgement
Deliver a planning dashboard
Attach scenarios, assumptions and an approval step

title: Build a small project plan you can verify
concept: A plan needs dependency logic and capacity limits, not just attractive dates. Calculate the earliest possible finish under explicit assumptions. A change in duration must propagate to dependent work rather than remain hidden in a cached report.
rules: Task A takes 2 days, B takes 3 after A, and C takes 1 after A. B and C can run in parallel. No staffing or safety-engineering decisions are automated.
edges: Add a dependency A after B: detect a cycle.
Increase A to 4 days: project duration becomes 7.
Only one worker available: parallel execution is no longer a valid assumption.
stages: Map deliverables and dependencies
Write each predecessor before drawing dates
Calculate the earliest finish
Use a small dependency graph and hand-check the critical chain
Build a change-aware plan
Compute finish times from input durations rather than typing static dates
Test a cycle and capacity change
Reject invalid dependency graphs; document resource assumptions
Rehearse stakeholder communication
Name an owner and uncertainty without inventing executive authority
Deliver a plan and retrospective template
Track actual work separately from estimates

title: Repair dirty records without inventing facts
concept: Cleaning is a policy decision with an audit trail. Duplicate IDs, blanks and invalid types are different problems. Preserve the original and reject ambiguous values rather than making a complete-looking table with invented numbers.
rules: IDs must be unique, amounts finite and non-negative; zero is valid. First occurrence wins only in this fixture; real conflicting records require review.
edges: Conflicting duplicate: send to a human instead of quietly selecting a value.
Blank amount is not zero.
Rejecting every unusual value can remove legitimate data; review the policy before generalising.
stages: Write a data dictionary
Specify identifier, amount and validation rules in plain language
Mark each dirty row manually
Establish accepted rows and rejection reasons before automating
Build a non-destructive cleaner
Return clean data and a reject log without overwriting the source
Test duplicates, blanks and zero
Use distinct reason codes so failures remain explainable
Audit the source and policy
Validate subject matter against primary tool documentation, not a misleading catalogue heading
Ship a repair kit and audit trail
Include the original, cleaned data, rejects and tests

title: Fit a regression and inspect its residuals
concept: Regression estimates a relationship between inputs and a numeric target. A synthetic straight line is useful for checking code, but perfect fit on a designed fixture is not a real-world benchmark. Compare with a mean baseline and preserve the future test example.
rules: Fit training pairs (1,5),(2,8),(3,11),(4,14). Test x=5 against y=17 only after fitting. Do not imply causal or production validity.
edges: All training x values equal: the simple slope is undefined.
Change the test target to 19: prediction stays 17 and absolute error becomes 2.
Use test y while fitting: identify leakage even if error falls.
stages: Define the regression target
Separate input availability from the future value being predicted
Compute a mean baseline
Use only training targets for the naive estimate
Fit and inspect a straight line
Calculate slope, intercept and residuals explicitly
Test outside the training range
Extrapolation needs caution even when this synthetic example succeeds
Compare model selection fairly
Choose metrics before comparing methods; do not optimise on the final test example
Ship a supervised experiment record
Document the fixture design and why zero error is not a general claim

title: Build a preprocessing step that cannot see the future
concept: Preprocessing learns parameters such as means from training data. Including test values in that calculation leaks information before fitting a predictor. Keep fitted parameters explicit so the boundary can be checked even in a tiny fixture.
rules: Fit a mean imputer on training values only, ignoring null. Transform train and test using that one mean; never refit on the test set.
edges: Including 100 in the fit would change the mean: detect the leakage.
All training values missing: stop and request a stated fallback policy.
A new extreme test value must not change stored training parameters.
stages: Mark the training boundary
Write down which rows the fitted transformation is allowed to inspect
Calculate the permitted mean
Use only the observed training values
Implement fit then transform
Return fitted parameters separately from transformed data
Inject an extreme test value
Demonstrate that training parameters do not change
Extend to time and class imbalance
Keep chronological splits and resampling inside training only
Ship a leakage-resistant pipeline contract
Attach tests for missingness, refit attempts and parameter provenance

title: Audit a tool with evidence, not an ethics slogan
concept: Responsible use is visible in test cases, approval boundaries and residual risks. A model can perform differently across languages, bandwidth conditions or data categories. Small samples reveal questions; they cannot certify fairness or legal compliance.
rules: Report error rates by explicitly supplied scenario group, disclose sample sizes and block release for unresolved critical privacy failures. These groups are test scenarios, not inferred sensitive identities.
edges: Remove the privacy failure: do not claim fairness from only two examples per group.
A missing group must be reported as untested, not assigned perfect accuracy.
A provider says safe: keep independent tests and a named human owner.
stages: Map affected people and data
Name who can be harmed and which inputs are sensitive
Design scenario-based checks
Include differing language and access conditions without inferring identities
Measure failures transparently
Report denominators and avoid hiding disparities behind an average
Apply an approval gate
A critical privacy failure blocks release even if other scores are high
Write residual risks and accountability
Keep responsibility with people; a model output is not a compliance opinion
Deliver a reviewable risk record
Include mitigations, owners, unresolved limits and review date

title: Measure whether a workflow actually saves time
concept: A productivity experiment must include setup, checking and repair. Comparing a polished assisted attempt with an unfamiliar manual attempt biases the result. Repeated tasks differ; report the actual sample and conditions rather than a universal percentage.
rules: Total assisted time equals draft plus checking plus rework. Keep all observations, including cases where assistance loses time. No private diary uploads or employee surveillance.
edges: Add 3 setup minutes: net saving changes to -2.
Drop the slowest assisted case: label cherry-picking, not improvement.
A task changes in complexity: record the confound rather than reusing a prior saving.
stages: Choose a voluntary recurring task
Define start/stop rules and a privacy-preserving log
Record a manual baseline
Keep task difficulty and output criteria comparable
Count the full assisted workflow
Include checking and repair rather than timing the first draft only
Stress-test the apparent saving
Add setup cost and inspect the change in the verdict
Build a sustainable work plan
Prioritisation is a choice with constraints, not a reason to monitor other people secretly
Deliver a measured recommendation
Report sample, conditions and a reversible next step

title: Join two datasets without multiplying the truth
concept: Joining datasets depends on key uniqueness and relationship cardinality. A many-to-many join can multiply rows and amounts without a syntax error. Check unmatched and repeated keys before summarising the merged table.
rules: Lookup keys must be unique for this many-to-one join. Preserve every order and report missing lookup keys rather than silently dropping orders.
edges: Duplicate a lookup key: reject ambiguous cardinality before joining.
Drop the unmatched order: report that data loss explicitly.
Quantity zero is a valid zero-value order under this fixture policy.
stages: Declare the join relationship
Write the unit of each table and the key cardinality
Trace matched and unmatched rows
Compute a known total without deleting unknown items
Build a checked merge
Validate uniqueness before combining records
Test duplicated and missing keys
Watch both row counts and monetary totals after the join
Handle nested and text fields
Flatten only with a documented mapping and preserve original IDs
Deliver a wrangling pipeline
Include row reconciliation, unknown-key policy and repeatability tests

title: Use a pipeline and a genuinely held-out set
concept: A library pipeline fits transformations and a predictor together, reducing accidental leakage. Cross-validation belongs inside the training partition. A final holdout is a one-time audit, not a tuning dashboard.
rules: This tiny separable synthetic fixture is a wiring test only. Fit StandardScaler and LogisticRegression on six rows; predict four held-out rows. Record versions and do not generalise the resulting score.
edges: Move a test point near the class boundary: inspect uncertainty instead of demanding a perfect score.
Scale on all rows before splitting: identify leakage.
Try another seed or a harder dataset: keep the new result even if performance drops.
stages: Reserve a final holdout
Write the split and allowed tuning procedure before fitting
Fit the simplest baseline
Compare against majority class and transparent rules
Compose preprocessing and model
Use a pipeline so training parameters stay within the correct partition
Inspect predictions and errors
A four-point synthetic success checks wiring, not field reliability
Compare validation schemes
Explain when random versus time-based splits are appropriate
Ship a versioned experiment bundle
Include parameters, held-out predictions, software versions and a model card

title: Make cleaning decisions testable with Pandas
concept: A cleaning script needs tests for preservation as well as removal. Missing values, duplicates and outliers have different meanings. A high value may be a legitimate transaction; automatically deleting it can distort the report.
rules: Drop exact duplicate IDs only in this fixture, fill missing units with the stated zero policy, and retain the legitimate 100-unit outlier. In real work, review conflicting duplicates and missing-value semantics first.
edges: A duplicate ID with a different amount needs review, not automatic first-row selection.
Changing the missing policy to unknown means the old zero-fill expected file is no longer authoritative.
Do not remove 100 just because it is far from the median.
stages: Write preservation invariants
Identify values that must survive cleaning, including a legitimate outlier
Inspect missingness and duplicates
Distinguish exact copies from conflicting records
Implement an explicit Pandas policy
Show each transformation and its affected row count
Test accidental data loss
Assert that the outlier survives and totals reconcile
Separate preparation from model fitting
Do not learn normalisation parameters from future data
Ship tests with the cleaner
Include expected rows, rationale and a reject/review policy

title: Create a campaign pack without invented performance
concept: Advertising work combines creative claims with measurement. A click-through rate is observed clicks divided by impressions; it does not establish sales lift or causality. Use consented assets and fictional performance data until a legitimate real test exists.
rules: Calculate CTR and cost per click from the supplied fixture. No protected-characteristic targeting, unauthorised tracking, fabricated testimonials or guaranteed returns.
edges: Zero clicks: CPC is undefined, not zero.
More clicks do not establish more profit without sales, costs and attribution evidence.
An AI-written testimonial is not a customer review.
stages: Define a truthful offer and audience
Use a real problem and approved claims, not sensitive-feature targeting
Build a factual creative brief
Link every price, feature and testimonial to permission and evidence
Calculate a campaign baseline
Reconcile observed denominators and costs before generating commentary
Challenge a flattering narrative
Separate clicks, sales, profit and causal lift
Package approval and disclosure
State asset rights, revisions and client approval before publication
Deliver a campaign evidence pack
Provide creative variants, checked metrics and no unsupported success claim

title: Make charts that tell the checked truth
concept: A chart is an argument about data. Bar lengths need a meaningful baseline, units and readable labels. Accessibility also needs a text alternative, not simply a contrast check. Inspect a deliberately truncated-axis specification before rendering a corrected chart.
rules: Values are fictional counts. A bar chart must start at zero for this exercise and include units and a text alternative. Metadata checks cannot prove the rendered chart is visually honest.
edges: Set baseline to 0 and add a descriptive text alternative: specification checks pass.
Swap category labels: values may total correctly while the chart is still wrong.
Colour alone must not distinguish categories.
stages: Choose a question and chart type
Match the encoding to comparison, distribution or change
Audit the supplied misleading spec
Identify what a truncated baseline exaggerates
Render an accessible chart
Use clear units, labels and a checked table alongside the image
Test misleading transformations
Try swapped labels, omitted rows and changed scales
Write a factual text alternative
Describe the observed values without inventing an explanation
Deliver a chart and decision brief
Include source, code, accessible description and limitations

title: Find clusters—and show why they are not facts
concept: Clustering groups points according to representation, scale and algorithm settings. The labels are arbitrary and do not establish natural categories, personality types or fair treatment of people. Use synthetic item coordinates to inspect stability without profiling anyone.
rules: Fit two KMeans clusters on six synthetic points with random_state=7 and n_init=10. Compare groups by member IDs, not arbitrary numeric label names.
edges: Change k to 3: the partition changes without revealing a newly discovered truth.
Rescale one coordinate by 100: repeat the experiment and explain representation sensitivity.
Do not label clusters as high-value people or employee risk.
stages: Describe features without human profiling
Define the toy item coordinates and their units
Inspect distance and scaling
Predict which points are near before fitting
Fit a reproducible clustering baseline
Keep parameters and compare membership instead of label IDs
Stress-test stability
Change scale, seed and k; retain disagreeing results
Distinguish discovery from validation
A visually neat plot does not establish objective categories
Ship a clustering exploration note
Describe alternatives and prohibit consequential profiling

title: Make Mula: useful work, honest offers
concept: An offer connects a narrow customer problem to a checked deliverable and a price hypothesis. AI does not create demand. Learn through real permission-based discovery where possible, but label rehearsals and never fabricate sales, experience or testimonials.
rules: Include selling, delivery, checking and support time. Payment-country eligibility must be verified before selling; no false residency, borrowed accounts or bypassing provider restrictions. Learning completion does not require earning money.
edges: Add a 10-unit refund: net becomes 15 and hourly return 3.75.
No paid order obtained: record zero earned income, not the hypothetical price.
A marketplace unavailable in the learner region is a stop condition until a legitimate route is verified.
stages: Find a problem through discovery
Ask three consenting potential users about their current workaround; keep simulations explicitly labelled
Build and break one sample
Choose checked reports, approved replies, verified content or a tiny web tool
Price the full workflow
Include selling and support time, fees, rework and refund assumptions
Check access and test the offer
Verify regional payout and identity rules, then use a small appropriate personalised approach with opt-outs
Deliver ethically and hand over
Define scope, approvals, rights, revisions, accounting boundaries and support
Decide from actual evidence
Record acceptance, refunds and net return if a paid pilot occurred; otherwise report the real market-test result without invention
reference: ILO Start and Improve Your Business
